new_misconceptions.message: It looks like the equations were added together rather than subtracted — because both equations have the same y-coefficient (4y), subtracting one from the other eliminates y straight away: (5x+4y) − (3x+4y) = 31−29, giving 2x = 2, so x = 1.

When subtracting the equations, watch which direction you go: taking equation 1 minus equation 2 gives 2x = 2, so x = 1 (positive) — if you got a negative value for x, check you subtracted the right-hand sides in the same order as the left-hand sides.

Once you have x = 1, substitute into either original equation keeping all coefficients as they appear: 5(1) + 4y = 31 gives 4y = 26 and y = 6.5 — using a coefficient of 3 for y instead of 4 is a copying slip that leads to the wrong answer.

After eliminating y you get 2x = 2, so you must divide both sides by 2 to find x = 1 — writing x = 2 means the division step was skipped; always divide the full equation by the coefficient of the variable you are solving for.

rationale: Minimal single-character edit: changed the coefficient of y in equation 1 from 3 to 4. With both equations sharing the coefficient 4y, subtracting equation 2 from equation 1 directly eliminates y: 2x = 2, x = 1; substituting back gives 4y = 26, y = 6.5. Both equations are now satisfied exactly (5(1)+4(6.5)=31, 3(1)+4(6.5)=29) and the stored solutions [1, 6.5] are correct. The original equation 2 and both constants (31 and 29) are unchanged.
